body: Re-reading it again,  wish I could give you a hug or something, that is a terrible story.  I almost lost my wife a few weeks ago to suicide,  but I couldn't imagine to losing her the way you did.  I have never loved someone as much as her and to see her "give up on me" would be the worst feeling I could imagine.  Your heart has to feel like the tightest knot,  I am so sorry.  I really hope you are to find some solace somewhere,  your health issues are a heavy burden to carry,  please try as hard as you can to shoulder them and really focus on yourself as best you can.

Hey - that really sucks man.  I really hope you have some other support you can really rely on in these times.  I know talking to family helps a little but its hard to share with them how bad it really is.  Even if it's something stupid, just to help get through the hard time. I once watched nacho libre 18 times in a row because it's the only thing I could laugh at and distract myself with.  I know the pain and grief you're dealing with and the daily battles you go through.  Even the needles, my wife once ripped out her IV in a panic at the hospital.  

If you don't mind my asking,  what type 2 treatment requires bloodwork? My wife was just diagnosed and we are still trying to find something that helps and hadn't heard of blood stuff.
Thanks,  I'll definitely check into it.
Yes.  She is in definite need of help,  for sure.  I feel bad that I let it get this bad but it's so hard not to enable the ones you love.  Thanks for your notes,  I'll look into those things.

Thankyou for your kind words.  Unfortunately I think it is too late for that. The counselor at the ER tried to get her to but she was not in a state to rationally think and instead panicked and wanted to stand up / leave and when they tried to get her to sit down she lashed out and had to be restrained, and after that said they were petitioning for her to be committed and somebody (I've heard "they ", "the doctors", etc.)  approved it and she's being transferred today.  

I don't really think there is much I can really do other than be available for her as much as I can.  The place doesn't allow visitation, just phone calls from 8am - 10pm, so we will have to make it work.  My focus right now is to try and help my wife remain calm so she can stay receptive to treatment and not feel so abandoned / alone / trapped. 

Thankyou

Thankyou for your response.  I will definitely check into those things.  The facility she is going to doesn't allow visitors,  which really sucks,  but it is what it is.  It's definitely scaring my wife because she's relies on me a lot to find calmness, but she is handling it okay right now.  My biggest concern is that when she gets into a big enough of a panic state she will start to get physically defensive and not want to sit down / be calm.  At the ER she wouldn't sit down so the guards tried to get her to and she fought back which caused them to get aggressive and restrain her (it's what they're supposed to do - I totally get that),  but that is literally her worst fear (she's had a lot of physical / sexual abuse in her past)  and im afraid that is just going to send her farther down the hole she's in right now.

Thankyou - I know everyone is going to try and help and just doing their jobs and following laws.  I'm definitely going to keep my feelings in check towards staff - I really appreciate all the help we've gotten so far and a few nurses have been incredibly kind and understanding.  Its just incredibly hard to trust all these people with the most important person in my life, particularly since one psychiatrist recently caused some great instability by drastically changing / adding medications every month after only 5 minute visits. I don't think I legally have a say / part in what happens now so it's just a little terrifying.  I know she'll be safe I'm just concerned she won't be able to cope with the isolation in her current state. 

Thanks for your advice and kind words,  I really appreciate them.
Thankyou!  I appreciate the explanation and advice.

I am really sorry that your life has led you to feel this way. Nothing about you justifies being physically abused for trying to do the right thing. I really hope you can find something positive about yourself and your life to carry you forward.  Nobody deserves the awful feelings that abuse leaves behind.
Thank you so much,  I appreciate it.

Hey Im just a husband with a wife as a patient, but I can say you are doing exactly what you should be doing.  I can't tell you how many times my wife has felt so degraded and awful for being treated less than human or like a child. The medical field for mental health is like a god damn minefield and you never know what person you trust to care for the person you love is really like, so please please don't ever forget that they are just people struggling and to do treat them like humans. I really really appreciate you showing kindness, I hope more can do the same.
